title: Miri Lint Report
description: The machine-readable report a Miri-conformance linter emits for one artifact. Draft: reconcile with the reference linter's output before pinning field constraints. The top-level version field is `schema_version` (per MIRI-CLI-010), never a per-format alias.

schema_version.description: Wire-schema version of this report document. An integer string — "1", "2" — compared numerically. Pinned because the convention lived only in prose and examples, and three surfaces had already diverged on it while all validating; this document is the most widely produced artifact in the ecosystem, so the drift would have propagated furthest from here.

artifact.description: Identity of the scored artifact (e.g. purl, version, filename)

checklist.description: Provenance of the check corpus scored against, so a report is never a naked score

checklist_version.description: The checklist stamp the definitions carry - the Specification Version header of the linter-checklist for this target, e.g. 0.2-draft. Distinct from standard_version, which is the RELEASE. The two move independently: 0.4.0 and 0.5.0 both carry stamp 0.2-draft while having inverted scoring semantics, so this field alone cannot tell two reports apart and checks_commit_sha is the discriminator that can.

checks_commit_sha.description: The commit the check definitions were read from, as a full 40-character sha. NOT a tag: a tag is a movable label and a sha is not, and the point of this field is that a reader can fetch the exact definitions a score was computed against. A tag moved after the fact would silently change what a published report points at. The human-legible release name goes in `standard_version`. Pattern requested by the miri-py team, whose argument was that a field named `commit_sha` permitting a tag is the same defect class this exchange was about - a name saying one thing and a value being another - and that a schema permitting a tag will eventually be given one.

standard_version.description: The MIRI release the report was scored against - the human-legible half of the pin, e.g. "0.5.0". Read from the standard's website/site.yaml at the pinned commit. A report previously named its checklist stamp and never the release, so a reader could not tell which version of the standard produced a score. Declared here rather than left as one implementation's extension: two linters inventing the same field under different names is the interoperability failure the wire schemas exist to prevent.

scores.description: The two-score model: a Conformance score and a Health score (see scoring-v1.json). A conformance score MUST be reported with its effective denominator and the excluded/forfeited counts; the number alone is not interpretable, because 80 out of 100 and 80 out of 58 are different claims.

conformance.description: Percentage of applicable weight earned. Bounded, because it was previously unbounded and a score of 480 over a denominator of 20 validated.

effective_denominator.description: Sum of the weights of the checks that APPLIED and could be evaluated — the denominator the conformance score was computed over. Both producer checklists make carrying this a MUST. Checks with `scoring: gate` are never part of it: they carry weight 0 and are preconditions rather than measurements, so they appear in `outcomes` and gate conformance without entering either side of the ratio. It was previously impossible to report, since `scores` had no field for it.

excluded.description: Count of checks excluded because their condition did not apply. Not-applicable is not a pass: these left both sides of the ratio. A statement of SCOPE — nothing about them is unknown.

forfeited.description: Count of checks the linter could not evaluate for lack of a declared capability (`network`, `previous-release`, `execution`). Arithmetically identical to an exclusion; epistemically not. A statement of IGNORANCE — the obligation applied and went unchecked, so the artifact may be violating it.

undetermined.description: Count of MUST checks that were forfeited and therefore leave conformance undetermined. Distinct from `forfeited`, which counts every forfeit at any level: a forfeited SHOULD costs coverage but not conformance.

grade.description: Grade band, or `undetermined` where a MUST check was FORFEITED — the obligation applied and went unassessed, so the artifact is neither known to conform nor known to fail. `undetermined` is NOT non-conformance. An EXCLUDED MUST never produces it: that obligation did not exist for this artifact.

allOf.description: A skipped check MUST name its reason from the closed set. Without this a linter could skip every hard check and report nothing about why, which is indistinguishable from having evaluated them.

must_failures.description: IDs of failing MUST checks. Non-empty means the artifact is NON-CONFORMING, and the root allOf rules enforce that rather than asserting it: a report could previously carry a failed MUST here and declare grade gold with conformance 100, and validate. Required rather than optional, because omitting the field was the other way to hide a failure. An empty array is correct when nothing failed.

allOf.description: A failing MUST makes an artifact non-conforming. The grade must say so and the score must respect the 74 cap. This is the rule `scoring: gate` delegates its entire effect to - a gate carries weight 0, so a failing one leaves no arithmetic trace and `must_failures` is its only representation - and until now nothing enforced it.
A non-conforming grade must name what failed.
